Holcim Elevate Roofing Systems for Winston-Salem Commercial Buildings

Holcim Elevate, the roofing products business formerly known as Firestone Building Products, manufactures single-ply membrane, coating, and insulation products that appear in commercial roof specifications we prepare for buildings across the Triad. We reference Elevate's current technical documentation when a project specification calls for its systems, the same way we do for any manufacturer named in a bid.

Product categories relevant to local specifications

Elevate's commercial catalog spans EPDM in black and white, TPO membrane in multiple thicknesses, and coating systems suited to roof restoration projects, along with polyisocyanurate insulation and cover board products designed to work within its tested assemblies. Each product carries its own technical data sheet specifying approved thickness, attachment method, and compatible accessories, and we build specifications from that current documentation rather than general familiarity with the product family.

Roof restoration projects on older industrial buildings around the area, where a sound existing membrane qualifies for coating rather than replacement, are a category where Elevate's coating product line frequently gets specified, provided a moisture survey confirms the underlying substrate is dry.

Warranty and program documentation

Elevate's warranty programs, like those of comparable manufacturers, generally require installation by contractors meeting program standards along with documentation of the installed system components. We state plainly that any specific program status or certification level should be verified directly through the manufacturer rather than taken from contractor representation alone, and we do not claim program standing we cannot document.

Warranty length and coverage scope depend on the specific system and program tier selected for a project, and those terms need confirmation in writing before a project is priced with warranty length as part of the value proposition.

Membrane selection by building condition

Older warehouse and manufacturing buildings around High Point and Thomasville with simple rooflines and established EPDM repair history are candidates for Elevate's EPDM product line when a reroof is needed, while buildings with higher rooftop traffic or specific reflectivity goals may point toward Elevate's TPO options instead. We assess each building's actual condition and use before recommending a specific product family within the manufacturer's broader catalog.

Compatibility between Elevate's membrane and insulation products and any existing deck or structural elements gets confirmed against the manufacturer's technical guidance before a specification is finalized, particularly on re-cover projects over decades-old construction.

  • Product data sheets referenced directly for every Elevate specification, not general product familiarity.
  • Moisture survey completed before recommending any Elevate coating system for restoration.
  • Membrane family matched to building condition, rooftop traffic, and reflectivity goals.
  • Warranty program terms confirmed in writing directly with the manufacturer.
  • Insulation and cover board compatibility checked against existing deck condition on re-cover projects.

Piedmont field conditions and Elevate systems

Hot-air welding on Elevate TPO membrane requires the same attention to Piedmont summer humidity and dew point as any single-ply system, affecting the practical daily installation window during peak summer months. Wind uplift performance for Elevate systems, per the manufacturer's published ratings, needs matching against each building's actual exposure category rather than treating a data sheet number as universally applicable.

For restoration coating projects, application timing similarly depends on measured dew point and surface moisture conditions rather than a fixed schedule, since coating applied over a damp substrate can fail to bond properly regardless of product quality.

Documentation practices for owners

We provide owners with the specific Elevate product data sheets referenced in a project specification, allowing independent verification of what is actually being proposed rather than relying on a summary description. This is particularly relevant for restoration coating projects, where the specific coating product, thickness, and recoat interval should be documented clearly before work begins.

Any field adjustment to a standard Elevate detail, driven by existing building conditions, gets documented and, where it affects warranty eligibility, discussed with the manufacturer's program representative rather than resolved informally.

Where Elevate fits among competing single-ply manufacturers

Owners evaluating an Elevate specification against a competing manufacturer's proposal should compare membrane thickness, reinforcement, and insulation package line for line rather than assuming equivalence based on brand reputation alone. We lay out that comparison plainly when asked, since two single-ply proposals naming different manufacturers can still result in a materially similar roof once the actual components are matched.

For buildings with restoration coating as a live option, we also compare the coating path against a full reroof honestly, since an Elevate coating system is not automatically the lower long-term cost once recoat cycles are factored against a new membrane's expected service life.

Questions about Holcim Elevate roofing systems

Is Holcim Elevate the same company as Firestone Building Products?

Elevate is the roofing products business previously known as Firestone Building Products, now operating under the Holcim Elevate name.

What roofing systems does Elevate manufacture?

Elevate's commercial line includes EPDM, TPO, restoration coatings, and related insulation and cover board products.

Does an Elevate specification guarantee a specific warranty length?

No. Warranty terms depend on the specific product and program tier selected, which should be confirmed directly with the manufacturer in writing.

Can an aging EPDM roof be restored with an Elevate coating system?

Sometimes, if a moisture survey confirms the substrate is dry and sound. We do not recommend coating without that verification.

Do you hold a specific certification level with Holcim Elevate?

We work from the manufacturer's current technical documentation for each project and recommend owners confirm any program standing directly with the manufacturer.
